finding: All20 anonymous Science HTTPS requests received Cloudflare Access302 before either Worker. Original hostname-wide Access application overlapped the new public portal.

decision.mechanism: Narrow the existing original self_hosted application public destinations to precisely the retained legacy paths; preserve original Worker destination and all authentication policy/identity-provider/session/cookie properties. No new bypass policy/application or account-wide change.
decision.fieldConsistency: Update legacy domain/self_hosted_domains consistently to the same bounded destinations if API requires. No bare science.561.group hostname may remain a matching protected public destination.
decision.protectedScope: Original Access outer authentication remains on every retained legacy path, including API, OAuth, vault, health, old feeds and retained assets; original Worker inner authentication remains unchanged.
decision.newPortalScope: Root, native publication feeds/assets/search/discovery/resources and ordinary native publication routes are public as explicitly requested and independently accepted.
decision.privateRefusalReceiving: Anonymous retained legacy paths should continue to show Access refusal/302. Do not remove existing Access to force observation of the inner401. Unchanged original Worker version/source proves preservation of its inspected inner guard; no authenticated private read is required or authorized by this review.

officialSources.claim: Specific paths and path wildcards are supported; hostname-wide configuration protects all paths.
Public destination URIs may contain domain/path wildcards; destinations replace deprecated self_hosted_domains.
Worker protection covers its routes while hostname-based matching controls matching URLs.

requiredReadback: Same original application id, Worker destination, policy id/content, IdP selections and unrelated security/session fields.
Exactly eight bounded public destinations; no bare hostname catchall or bypass policy.
Public root/native artifacts return correct200 bytes while original legacy paths still require original Access.

limitations: No authenticated login, grant, authoring or private read is performed.
Protected legacy public asset paths may remain behind the existing Access gate; this is preserved predecessor behavior, not a new public L-Space release.
